explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/636 (Erdős–Faudree–Sós): if an n-vertex G has no clique or independent set on ≫ log n vertices, must G contain ≫ n^{5/2} induced subgraphs pairwise differing in number of vertices or edges? Proved by Kwan–Sudakov. The Lean statement: for every C > 0 there is γ > 0 such that for large n, every G on Fin n with ω(G), α(G) < C log n has a family of ≥ γ n^{5/2} vertex sets pairwise distinguished by size or induced edge count. Quantifying 'no clique/independent set on ≫ log n vertices' as 'below C log n, for each fixed C, with γ depending on C' is the standard reading. Faithful.
